method: Exact archived full-context requests, no guard or sampling; full games use identical definitions and general tactics.

definitions_and_rules.players: Two opponents play: you control O (the letter O, drawn as a circle); your opponent controls X (the letter X, drawn as a cross). Marks are ownership labels, not numbers.
definitions_and_rules.board: There are nine cells in a 3 by 3 square. Columns A, B, C run left to right. Rows 1, 2, 3 run top to bottom. A cell ID combines its column and row; A1 is top-left and C3 bottom-right.
definitions_and_rules.symbols: In the board, X means a cell occupied by your opponent, O means a cell occupied by you, and . means an empty cell. Board arrays list rows top to bottom and cells left to right.
definitions_and_rules.turns: The starting_player field identifies who went first. Players alternate one placement per turn. The player_to_move field identifies whose turn it is now.
definitions_and_rules.legal_move: A placement puts the current player's mark in exactly one empty cell. Occupied cells cannot be selected. There are no captures, removals, moving existing marks, passes, or hidden information.
definitions_and_rules.winning: A player wins immediately upon occupying all three cells of any complete row, column, or diagonal. Winning ends the game before another turn. The eight winning lines are listed below.
definitions_and_rules.draw: If every cell is occupied and neither player has won, the game is a draw. There are no other draw conditions or move limits.
definitions_and_rules.objective: Choose a legal move that gives O the best final outcome against an opponent trying to achieve the best outcome for X. O winning is better than drawing, and drawing is better than O losing.
definitions_and_rules.tactical_terms: An immediate winning move completes a winning line now. A threat is a move that would complete a winning line on the threatening player's next turn. Blocking occupies that threat's empty cell. A fork creates two distinct immediate winning moves on a future turn, so one defensive placement cannot block both. Center means B2; corners mean A1,C1,A3,C3; sides mean B1,A2,C2,B3.

strategy: Take an immediate win if one exists.
Otherwise prevent the opponent from winning on their next turn if possible.
Otherwise consider creating a fork, provided the opponent cannot win first.
Otherwise prevent an opponent fork; consider how both players can respond to each candidate move.
When outcomes are otherwise equal, prefer the center, then corners, then sides. Tactical necessities take priority over these location preferences.

move.instructions: Choose the legal placement that gives O the best game outcome. Apply the supplied rules and general tactics to the complete position. Evaluate possible replies by X. Each choice describes only a placement, not its quality.

choice_description_template: Place your O mark in empty cell {cell}.
